governing_thought: CRDB positions its own output within a defined 6-phase Reference Integrated Data and Web Platform SDLC -- raising independently-scored coverage of phase 1 (Requirements Elicitation & Analysis) from roughly 35% to 70% and phase 2 (Functional Analysis & Solution Design) from roughly 40% to 80% -- and hands over five concrete, checkable ready-to-build artifacts plus a clear Content Writer / Software Developer role split, so that whoever builds next can begin implementation immediately instead of repeating discovery, without this section presuming what that next project's procurement will actually say.

narrative_scqa.situation: The platform's development follows a recognized six-phase reference lifecycle -- Requirements Elicitation & Analysis, Functional Analysis & Solution Design, Implementation, System Integration Verification & Validation, Deployment & Operational Transition, and Operations/Maintenance/Continuous Improvement -- synthesized from established industry practice (TOGAF, IBM data architecture guidance, the Australian National Archives' interoperability guidance, and BrowserStack's web-application lifecycle guidance).
narrative_scqa.complication: Scored independently against that reference lifecycle's own constituent activities, coverage of the first two phases is partial without CRDB's work counted (roughly 35% and 40%). Without a documented, checkable handoff, whoever builds the platform next would have to re-derive requirements analysis and solution design essentially from zero -- discovering only after starting that the foundational work already exists elsewhere, unattributed and unusable.
narrative_scqa.question: What must this section establish so that CRDB's completed work functions as a real starting baseline for the next phase, rather than a set of documents nobody is required to use?
narrative_scqa.answer: It must state CRDB's phase-by-phase coverage lift in the reference lifecycle (phase 1 to roughly 70%, phase 2 to roughly 80%), name the five ready-to-build artifacts that supply that lift with their real scale, and set out how Content Writer and Software Developer roles should use them -- all stated as risk-reducing groundwork for whichever project follows, never as a claim about what that project's own scope of work will say.

argument_units.claim: CRDB's delivered output corresponds to phases 1 and 2 of the six-phase Reference Integrated Data and Web Platform SDLC, raising independently-scored coverage substantially: phase 1 (Requirements Elicitation & Analysis) from roughly 35% to roughly 70%, and phase 2 (Functional Analysis & Solution Design) from roughly 40% to roughly 80%.
argument_units.grounds: The TOR70 SDLC storyline analysis (2026-08-26_TOR70-SDLC-storyline-for-DCCE-briefing.md) scores coverage twice against the same reference lifecycle's own constituent activities -- once without CRDB's deliverables counted, once with them counted as satisfying specific activities -- and reports the coverage lift explicitly in its 'Coverage re-scored with CRDB adopted as baseline' table: stage 1 from ~35% to ~70%, stage 2 from ~40% to ~80%, driven by named CRDB deliverables (stakeholder interviews, service business cases, demand analysis, the data catalog and asset audit, the DRD, the CDM, glossary, metadata standard, sitemap v9 and its UX evaluations, the WP5 governance framework, the WP7 gap analysis).
argument_units.warrant: Because these percentages come from a structured, activity-by-activity scoring against a documented, industry-anchored reference methodology -- not a self-assessment or a round-number claim -- they support treating CRDB's output as a genuine, checkable functional handoff into phase 3, rather than an informal head start whose value the reader has to take on faith.
argument_units.application_to_design: Name the reference lifecycle's six phases and state both coverage percentages explicitly in the section's opening, framed as CRDB's position within a defined lifecycle rather than as a vague progress claim.

argument_units.claim: This coverage lift exists specifically to close a 'Discovery Trap': without a documented baseline handoff, whoever builds the platform next would have to re-derive requirements analysis and solution design from zero, at cost, even though that work already exists.
argument_units.grounds: The TOR70 analysis document's 'Building on CRDB instead of starting over' section states plainly that a scope of work written without reference to CRDB's deliverables 'instructs the incoming contractor to survey the data estate, build a data inventory, define categories, write system requirements, design the data architecture and design the sitemap, as though none of that had been done' -- and names the resulting cost as double: the contractor is paid to re-derive work that already exists, and the artifacts CRDB deliberately deferred to the build phase risk becoming nobody's job.
argument_units.warrant: Because a builder operating without this baseline pays twice for the same analysis and design work, and risks losing track of what CRDB deliberately deferred rather than omitted, stating the risk in general terms -- what happens to a builder who does not inherit this baseline -- keeps the argument useful regardless of what any specific future procurement ends up saying, satisfying the plan's explicit constraint against presuming the next TOR's content.
argument_units.application_to_design: State the risk generically as what happens to a builder who starts without this baseline, never by naming or describing any specific next contract or its clauses.

argument_units.claim: CRDB hands over five ready-to-build artifacts, each independently produced and independently checkable: Sitemap v9 (38 nodes across 4 categories), DRD v2 (75 requirements, 13 deliverables, 9 service briefs, 12 data specs), the Node Content Storyboard v2 (38-page wireframes with Source-Content Mapping), the WP6 Service Business Narratives, and the CDM/DMF (8 domains, 12-field metadata standard, 74-term glossary).
argument_units.grounds: Sitemap v9 and its 38-node, 4-category structure is the companion node list underlying the DRD (per NCAIF_Detailed_Sitemap_v9.md and the plan's own figures). The DRD v2 delta note (2026-08-20-WP4-Developer-Ready-Design-Requirements-Specification-v2.md) confirms 75 requirements after the v9 delta pass, and confirms the deliverable count directly: 'Net deliverable count: 14 -> 13' following the DEL-2/DEL-13 merge; service-briefs-v2.csv and the data-specs count were carried forward unchanged this session. The WP5 Data Management Framework Report confirms the CDM's '8 functional logical domains' and states directly that 'Glossary v5 contains 74 canonically defined terms in both Thai and English.'
argument_units.warrant: Because each artifact was independently produced by a named prior work package against a checkable source document, and its scale figures are drawn from those documents' own verification statements rather than restated from memory, presenting them as a numbered list with real scale lets the reader verify the handoff instead of accepting a general claim about 'artifacts delivered.'
argument_units.application_to_design: Render as the required numbered list, one line per artifact naming its concrete scale (node/requirement/domain/term counts), with no per-page storyboard detail or DRD relationship-table content, per the section's exclusions.

argument_units.claim: A clear Content Writer / Software Developer role split governs how these artifacts should be used: Content Writer responsibility covers drafting the content that closes the identified content gaps against the Storyboard; Software Developer responsibility covers building CMS validation rules, data pipelines, and interface work against the DRD.
argument_units.grounds: The plan brief states this split directly: Content Writer closes the content gaps per Storyboard v2; Software Developer builds CMS validation rules, data pipelines, and UI per DRD v2. The TOR70 analysis document's governance section makes the underlying reason explicit -- distinguishing what 'Content Staff,' 'Data Stewards,' and 'Data Custodians' each need from the platform, and warning against a single contractor becoming the de facto product owner or inventing business logic that was never validated ('Logic Invention').
argument_units.warrant: Because the ready-to-build artifacts only reduce discovery and re-derivation risk if the people using them follow the role boundaries the artifacts were designed around, stating the split as direct guidance for how to use the handed-over artifacts -- not as a description of what any specific next contract will require of named job titles -- keeps this conclusion actionable while honoring the plan's hard constraint against presuming next-TOR content.
argument_units.application_to_design: State the two roles and their scope directly, tied to the artifacts named in arg-03 (Storyboard for Content Writer, DRD for Software Developer), followed by a brief, generic scoping note for the next project phase ahead of the governance detail that belongs in section 4.4.
